key_insight: Selenium alloying and air annealing suppress residual metallic tellurium in amorphous TeOx films, enabling thin-film solar cells with approximately 1.87% efficiency.
engineering_relevance: Chemical-state control offers a route to improve oxide-derived photovoltaic absorbers fabricated by scalable vacuum deposition.
method: Thermally evaporate a 90:10 wt% TeO₂:Se powder mixture.
Anneal films in air at 225 °C for up to 9 hours.
Integrate an 80 nm absorber into an ITO/ZnO/TeOx:Se/MoOx/Ag device.
evidence_signal: Optimized devices achieved 0.50 V open-circuit voltage, 8.50 mA/cm² short-circuit current density, 0.44 fill factor, and photocurrent response from 300–1000 nm; film analysis showed residual metallic Te reduced to approximately 0.4%.
watch_item: The 9-hour annealing step may constrain manufacturing throughput, while long-term stability and large-area reproducibility are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Amorphous selenium-alloyed TeOx thin-film solar cells
